title: Add vortex timezone skills and command
creator: NativLevy1
summaryParagraphs: This PR adds Vortex timezone guidance and a command for conversion work. It introduces a convert-vortex command, a new Vortex skill, and a conversion recipe reference.

It also extends both backend-coding and frontend-coding skills with timezone reference documents, creating a shared standard for how agents should reason about dates and timezones across the stack. All changed files are markdown.

findings.text: Since you control your own workflow, unlike spontaneous modal invocation, it's a good opportunity to provide here all the quality steps that you could imagine. You may perform more validation on start whether this is a good candidate for a Vortex flow. On end, you can run your own checklist to validate some known mis-message and quality gates, like, for example, the existence of testing, the correctness of the final DAG, etc.

findings.title: The conversion workflow is currently authored twice. convert-vortex.md defines a 6-step sequence ...
findings.text:
The conversion workflow is currently authored twice. convert-vortex.md defines a 6-step sequence and conversion-recipe.md defines an overlapping 8-step sequence plus the audit, so the command and the recipe are both steering the same ordered process. The result is that there is no single source of truth

The cleaner shape is to keep the workflow in exactly one file: the canonical ordered steps, with every validation and audit check inlined as a gate the run must pass. Everything else becomes leaf content the workflow pulls in on demand — one knowledge doc per step (or topic) for the "how"

findings.text:
Since it's a workflow, to have a better guarantee that all the steps are indeed executed, consider asking it upfront to first put all the tasks into the to-do list using the ToDoWrite tool

From that part, the harness is very good at following tasks and the user gets better visibility Into the process.
